topics.title: Acids, Bases and Indicators
topics.subject: chemistry
outcomes: Identify common acids and bases found at home and in the laboratory.
Describe the effect of acids and bases on litmus paper and other indicators.
State the pH scale and relate pH values to acidity, neutrality and basicity.
Describe neutralisation as the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water.

body.text: Acids and bases are two important groups of substances. Acids have a sour taste (like lemon juice and vinegar), turn blue litmus paper red, and have pH values below 7. Bases (also called alkalis when they dissolve in water) are bitter and slippery (like soap), turn red litmus paper blue, and have pH values above 7. Pure water is neutral, with a pH of 7.

An indicator is a substance that changes colour depending on whether it is placed in an acid or a base. Common indicators include litmus paper, universal indicator, and phenolphthalein. Universal indicator shows a range of colours across the pH scale, from red (strong acid) through green (neutral) to purple (strong base).

Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base. The products are a salt and water. For example, hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium chloride (common salt) and water. Neutralisation is used to treat acid soils (by adding lime) and to relieve excess stomach acid (using antacids).
